recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中多顆偏心核、細胞質豐富灰藍、核周有淡染區的漿細胞，部分細胞核較大、染色質較細緻，呈未成熟外觀。背景的紅血球堆疊成錢串狀（rouleaux），提示血中有大量單株免疫球蛋白，符合多發性骨髓瘤。
features: Increased plasma cells, many with eccentric round to oval nuclei and abundant grey-blue cytoplasm
Perinuclear hof (Golgi zone) visible in several cells
Some plasma cells show enlarged nuclei with finer chromatin and relatively higher N:C ratio, suggesting immature/atypical forms; nucleoli are not sharply resolved at this focus
Occasional cell with a pale, vacuolated cytoplasmic area
Prominent rouleaux formation of red cells in the background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows increased plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, abundant grey-blue cytoplasm and perinuclear clearing. A subset display atypical features, including enlarged nuclei, finer chromatin and a higher nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Red cells show prominent rouleaux formation, reflecting increased serum paraprotein. Image focus limits assessment of nucleoli. Findings are consistent with a plasma cell neoplasm (multiple myeloma); quantification of plasma cells on the full aspirate and core biopsy, with light chain restriction studies, is required.

ddx.vs: Reactive plasma cells are mature, usually <10% of marrow cells, polytypic and perivascular, without nuclear immaturity or marked rouleaux.
LPL shows a spectrum of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes and plasma cells with an IgM paraprotein and MYD88 L265P, rather than a predominantly plasma cell population.
Plasmablastic lymphoma cells are larger immunoblast-like cells with prominent central nucleoli, high Ki-67 and often EBER positivity, usually without an M protein.
Osteoblasts occur in clusters with the hof located away from the nucleus, and lack rouleaux-associated paraproteinemia.
